title_en: Your Team Copies All of You, Including the Parts You'd Rather It Didn't
title_zh: 你的團隊會複製完整的你，包括你不希望他們學的那部分
short_en: Your Team Copies All of You
excerpt_en: Duplication is the whole point of this business, and it doesn't stop at your strengths. If your team keeps attracting people and losing them, look at what you are modelling when you are not on stage.
excerpt_zh: 複製是這個事業的核心，而它不會只複製你的優勢。如果你的團隊一直吸引人、又一直留不住人，看看你不在台上的時候，示範的是什麼。
description_en: Teams duplicate their leader's weaknesses as faithfully as their strengths. Why patching yourself rarely works, and how a system and the right partners cover the gaps instead.
description_zh: 團隊複製領袖劣勢的忠實程度，跟複製優勢一模一樣。為什麼補自己的短板很少奏效，以及如何用系統和對的夥伴補上缺口。
keywords: duplication, leadership blind spots, team retention, direct selling plateau, follow-up system, strengths and weaknesses, Mikael Chew, 知己
blocks: p
Duplication is the whole point of this business. You do something, your partners copy it, their partners copy them, and the work spreads further than you could ever carry it alone.
複製是這個事業的核心。你做一件事，夥伴照著做，夥伴的夥伴再照著做，事業就能延伸到你一個人永遠扛不到的地方。
p
We talk about it as if it only applies to the good parts. It doesn't. Your team copies everything it sees you do, and everything it sees you skip.
我們談複製的時候，好像它只複製好的那部分。不是的。你的團隊會複製他們看到你做的每一件事，也會複製他們看到你略過的每一件事。
h2
The pattern behind most plateaus
大多數瓶頸背後的規律
p
Picture a leader who is brilliant in front of a room. Great trainer, great speaker, everybody leaves her meetings fired up. New people join her team all the time.
想像一位站在台前非常出色的領袖。她培訓得好、講得好，每個人參加完她的會議都熱血沸騰。新人不斷加入她的團隊。
p
Now picture what happens on day four, when a new partner has a question and nobody calls. Or on day ten, when the excitement has worn off and nobody checks in.
再想像一下第四天：一位新夥伴有問題，卻沒有人打電話給他。或是第十天：興奮感退了，也沒有人來關心。
p

Her team learned from her, so they are brilliant in front of a room too. The follow-up was never modelled, so it never got copied. People keep coming in through the front door and leaving quietly through the back.
她的團隊是跟她學的，所以他們在台前也很出色。但跟進從來沒有被示範過，所以也從來沒有被複製。人從前門不斷進來，又從後門悄悄離開。
p
From the outside it looks like a recruiting problem, so the team recruits harder. The leak keeps going, because its source is what the leader models.
從外面看，這像是招募的問題，所以團隊更努力招募。但漏洞一直都在，因為它的源頭，是領袖示範了什麼。
quote
Know yourself.
知己。
Sun Tzu
《孫子兵法》
h2
The honest list
那份誠實的清單
p
Most of us know our strengths very well. Our blind spots are blind for a reason. So write them down where you can't avoid them.
我們都很清楚自己的優勢，而盲點之所以叫盲點，是有原因的。所以，把它們寫在一個你躲不開的地方。
p

Take a sheet of paper and draw a line down the middle. Strengths on the left. Weaknesses on the right. Give the right-hand column twice as long as the left, and write the things you'd rather not admit, not the safe answers you'd give in a job interview.
拿一張紙，在中間畫一條線。左邊寫優勢，右邊寫劣勢。右邊那欄，花左邊兩倍的時間寫，寫那些你不太想承認的，而不是面試時拿來講的安全答案。
p
Then do the uncomfortable part. Look at your team and ask which of those weaknesses they have already copied.
然後做最不舒服的那一步：看看你的團隊，問自己，這些劣勢他們已經複製了哪幾個？
h2
Don't patch yourself. Build around the gap.
不要補自己，在缺口周圍建系統
p
The usual advice is to fix your weaknesses. Go on courses, force yourself to love spreadsheets, become a different person. Most leaders who try that end up tired and only slightly better.
常見的建議是：去補你的短板。去上課，逼自己愛上試算表，變成另一個人。大多數這樣努力的領袖，最後都累壞了，也只是好了一點點。
p
A better question is how to make the weakness stop mattering. There are three ways, and most gaps need one of them.
更好的問題是：怎麼讓這個劣勢不再造成影響？方法有三種，大多數缺口用得上其中一種。
ul

A system. If you forget follow-ups, stop relying on memory. Put every new partner into your calendar with reminders on day 1, 4, 7, 14 and 30, each with a short note of what to say. The calendar remembers so you don't have to.
一套系統。如果你總是忘記跟進，就不要再依賴記憶。把每一位新夥伴放進日曆，在第1、4、7、14、30天設提醒，每個提醒附上一句該說什麼。日曆記得，你就不需要記得。
A helper. If admin drains you, hand it to someone who finds it easy. Paying for a few hours of help is usually cheaper than the opportunities you lose while drowning in paperwork.
一位幫手。如果行政工作讓你精疲力盡，交給覺得這件事很輕鬆的人。花錢請幾個小時的幫忙，通常比你被文書工作淹沒時錯過的機會便宜。

A partner with the opposite strength. Some people love one-to-one care, track every detail without being asked, and make sure nobody falls through the cracks. Find them, value them, and let them lead that part of the team.
一位優勢跟你相反的夥伴。有些人天生喜歡一對一關懷，不用提醒就會追蹤每一個細節，確保沒有人被遺漏。找到他們、重視他們，讓他們帶領團隊的那一部分。
p

Once the gaps are covered, put most of your week back into what you do best. For the leader in our picture, that means more training and more time on stage, with the system and the detail people catching everyone she brings in.
缺口補上之後，把一週大部分的時間放回你最擅長的事。對我們想像中的那位領袖來說，就是更多培訓、更多時間在台上，而系統和細節型的夥伴，會接住她帶進來的每一個人。
h2
Model the thing you want copied
示範你希望被複製的東西
p
There is one more step. Your team copies what it sees, so let them see the system working.
還有最後一步。你的團隊複製的是他們看到的，所以，讓他們看到系統在運作。
p
Show new leaders your calendar. Introduce the partner who handles follow-up as a leader in their own right. Talk openly about the things you are bad at and how you have covered them.
讓新領袖看看你的日曆。把負責跟進的夥伴，當成一位真正的領袖來介紹。公開談你不擅長什麼，以及你是怎麼補上的。
p
That honesty does something useful. It gives everyone on your team permission to admit their own gaps, and a clear way to deal with them.
這種坦白很有用。它讓團隊裡每一個人，都可以承認自己的缺口，也知道該怎麼處理。
p
So here's the question to sit with. If your team copied you exactly as you are today, which column would hold them back?
所以，好好想想這個問題：如果你的團隊完完全全複製今天的你，會是哪一欄拖住他們？

cta.h_en: Build a team that runs without you
cta.h_zh: 打造一支不靠你也能運轉的團隊
cta.p_en: Duplication, systems and knowing yourself run through the whole of my book, from the first chapter to the last.
cta.p_zh: 複製、系統、了解自己，是我這本書從第一章到最後一章的主線。
